brief:
Democrats have moved to the center on major policy issues since the last presidential election, adjusting their positions on Gaza, transgender rights, and other contentious matters in response to voter sentiment, Al Jazeera English reported. The party's candidates have recalibrated their messaging across multiple fronts as they seek to appeal to a broader electorate ahead of the upcoming vote.

The shifts reflect evolving Democratic strategies on questions that have fractured their coalition, from support for Israel's military operations to the scope of transgender protections in law and policy. Candidates have adopted more cautious or modified rhetoric compared to earlier Democratic platforms, attempting to balance different wings of the party while addressing concerns raised by various voter groups.
dek: From trans rights to Israel's war on Gaza, the party's candidates have responded to voter shifts on a slew of issues.
title: Democrats shift stance on Gaza, trans rights ahead of election
